ch01.alt: A black-and-white photograph of a crowd of men in caps and tunics massed in a courtyard before a two-story building, a broad white banner or awning stretched overhead; a few figures in the foreground carry staves.
ch01.caption: The Shanghai Workers' Pickets before the general headquarters of the third armed uprising, March 1927.

ch01.before: Just as the Shanghai workers were celebrating
ch01.alt: A black-and-white photograph of a long file of workers in caps and dark tunics marching down a city street lined with onlookers.
ch01.caption: The Shanghai Workers' Pickets setting out to join a citizens' rally, 27 March 1927.

ch02.before: Mainly, though, Section One set up various working offices
ch02.alt: A black-and-white photograph looking down a narrow brick lane at the doorway and upper-floor bay window of a shikumen terraced house in the former French Concession.
ch02.caption: The former site of the Central Military Commission's offices during Zhou Enlai's time as its secretary in Shanghai: Lafayette Lane, off Rue Lafayette in the former French Concession (now 553 Central Fuxing Road).

ch02.before: At first the Standing Committee of the Central Political Bureau
ch02.alt: A grainy black-and-white photograph of a Shanghai street frontage: a shopfront hung with Chinese signboards, and a period automobile parked at the curb with two men beside it.
ch02.caption: The former site of the CCP Central Political Bureau's offices in Shanghai, 1928–1931: 477 Yunnan Road (now 171–173 Yunnan Central Road). [The building number is given as 447 in the text of this chapter and as 477 on this photograph in the source; both are reproduced as printed.]

ch03.before: Chen Geng, Zhou Yiqun, and Lu Dongsheng left Shantou
ch03.alt: A worn black-and-white photograph of a young woman holding a small boy of two or three against her side; both look off to one side.
ch03.caption: Wang Genying and Chen Zhifei, Shanghai, 1931.

ch04.before: Liu Ding had married a fellow student
ch04.alt: A black-and-white studio portrait of a young woman with short, side-parted hair, wearing a light high-collared gown, gazing slightly to one side.
ch04.caption: Wu Xianqing.

ch04.before: Ke Lin (1900-1991) was a native of Haifeng
ch04.alt: A black-and-white head-and-shoulders portrait of a young man with dark hair combed back, in a light Western suit jacket, waistcoat, and tie.
ch04.caption: Ke Lin (1900–1991).

ch04.before: Chen Yangshan was born Cheng Yangshan
ch04.alt: A black-and-white half-length photograph of an elderly bald man in an open-collared short-sleeved shirt, seated outdoors on a bench before trees, one forearm resting on the arm of the seat.
ch04.caption: Chen Yangshan (1906–1991).

ch05.before: In this elegy for Comrade Li Kenong, Dong Biwu voiced a deep grief
ch05.alt: A page of fluid cursive Chinese calligraphy, eight lines of verse in dark ink followed by a dated signature to the left.
ch05.caption: Dong Biwu's elegy for Li Kenong, in his own hand, February 1962. (Source label: “Dong Biwu's elegy mourning Li Kenong.”)

ch05.before: Qian Zhuangfei (1896–1935), whose original name was Zhuangqiu
ch05.alt: A grainy black-and-white photograph of a young man in a Western suit and tie seated in a wicker armchair on a plant-filled veranda, one leg crossed over the other, looking toward the camera.
ch05.caption: Qian Zhuangfei in the late 1920s.

ch09.before: In May 1930 a national Soviet congress
ch09.alt: A black-and-white photograph of an elderly bald man in glasses and a light jacket bending over an open book or folio at a cluttered desk, tall bookshelves behind him.
ch09.caption: Li Yimang at work in his study (1984).

ch10.before: After Luo Yinong was arrested he was held
ch10.alt: A black-and-white photograph of a young woman in a checked jacket holding a small child in a flowered dress against her lap, both looking toward the camera against a dark ground.
ch10.caption: Li Wenyi, holding Yang Zhihua's daughter Qu Duyi.

ch11.before: On the afternoon of 24 August 1929, Peng Pai
ch11.alt: A black-and-white photograph of a Shanghai lane-house building, the arrest site.
ch11.caption: The place where Peng Pai and the others were arrested: No. 12 Jingyuan Li, Xinwen Road, Huxi district, Shanghai. (Label from the source; caption by the translator.)

ch12.before: Very soon our side had a complete grasp
ch12.alt: A black-and-white photograph of a building entrance with a curved iron balcony, the archway sign reading Hehe Fang.
ch12.caption: The mouth of Hehe Fang on Avenue Joffre, Shanghai. (Label from the source; caption by the translator.)

ch12.before: Toward ten o'clock the night before last
ch12.alt: A scanned clipping of the Chinese newspaper Shi Bao reporting the killing.
ch12.caption: The Shanghai papers Shi Bao and Shishi Xinbao report the suppression of the traitor Bai Xin, 13 November 1929. (From the source; caption by the translator.)

ch12.before: The foreign-language papers, for their part
ch12.alt: A scanned clipping of the English-language North China Daily News headlined 'Political Murder in Shanghai.'
ch12.caption: The Shanghai English-language North China Daily News reports the suppression of the traitor Bai Xin, 13 November 1929. (From the source; caption by the translator.)
